transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I'm really only here because my family insisted I see a doctor after I lost some weight recently. Personally, I think they are overreacting and it's not a big deal, but I promised them I would come.
Did you lose this weight intentionally, and how do you feel about the prospect of gaining any of it back?

Yes, I lost the weight intentionally by strictly controlling my diet, and I worked really hard to get here. The thought of gaining any of it back is absolutely terrifying to me. I honestly cannot let myself put any weight back on.
Do you ever experience episodes where you eat a very large amount of food in a short period of time and feel like you've completely lost control over your eating?
No, I never do that. I actually do the complete opposite and strictly limit how much I eat. I make sure I only eat very small portions so I never lose control.
When you look in the mirror, how do you perceive your current body shape and weight?

When I look in the mirror, I still see so many areas that look way too big, especially my stomach and thighs. Even though everyone tells me I'm too thin, I just see someone who still looks flabby and needs to be much slimmer.
Besides restricting your food, do you use other methods to control your weight, such as exercising excessively, taking laxatives, or making yourself throw up?

No, I don't do any of those things. I have never used laxatives, made myself throw up, or forced myself to exercise excessively. I only manage my weight by strictly controlling and restricting what I eat.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets all core DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for Anorexia Nervosa: restriction of energy intake leading to weight loss (with family expressing concern that they are too thin), an intense fear of gaining weight, and a significant disturbance in body image (perceiving themselves as 'flabby' and 'too big' despite being thin). Binge eating and purging behaviors have been ruled out. Therefore, the diagnosis of Anorexia Nervosa is confirmed.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits key features of Anorexia Nervosa, including intentional significant weight loss, an intense fear of gaining weight, and a severely distorted body image (perceiving themselves as overweight despite others pointing out they are too thin). They also deny any binge eating or purging behaviors, relying solely on severe restriction of food intake.
